title: Tech Note: Removing Win32s
author: Christopher Chapman
featured_technology: Win32s (32-bit Windows compatibility layer for Windows 3.1/WfW)

historical_commentary.text: This note gives step-by-step DOS/SYSTEM.INI instructions for manually removing a corrupted or conflicting Win32s installation (the 32-bit thunking layer that let 4D, 4D Client, and 4D Server run under 16-bit Windows 3.1/Windows for Workgroups) so it can be cleanly reinstalled; Win32s and 16-bit Windows 3.1/WfW have been completely obsolete for decades, making this note of historical interest only.
related_updates: Win32s and Windows 3.1/Windows for Workgroups have been obsolete since the late 1990s, superseded by native 32-bit (and later 64-bit) Windows versions starting with Windows 95/NT
4D has not required any 16-bit-to-32-bit thunking layer since Windows 95/NT became the baseline, and modern 4D runs as a native 32-bit/64-bit Windows application
